the identification of a tumor antigen that can serve as a biomarker in the early detection of colorectal cancer.
the expression profiles of the C2-O-sLe(x) antigen and C2Gn-T1 mRNA in human colorectal cancers and liver metastasis.
the expression of C2-O-SLe(x) in colorectal adenoma and cancer.

C2-O-sLeX expression in human colorectal cancer cells and liver tumors is significantly higher than that in normal tissues and that C2-OsLeX expression is associated with the malignant progression of human colorectal cancers.

C2-O-sLe(x), detected by the CHO131 mAb, was found to be a highly expressed tumor-associated antigen in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression and in the metastasis of colorectral adenocarcinoma to the liver.

the high affinity selectin ligand C2O-sLex is highly expressed in human adenocarcinoma of the colon and metastatic liver lesions, and that the mRNA transcripts of the enzyme core2 β-1.6-N-acetyl-glucosaminyl-transferase (C2GN1), which synthesizes C2O-sLeX, are significantly increased in adenocarcinomatous colorectal tissues compared to normal colorectum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C2-O-slex is a potential tumor marker for colorectal adenocaricnomas.
C2-O-slex is a potential biomarker of metastasis in human colorectal cancer.
the C2-O-sLe(x) antigen, which is a ligand for the selectin family of adhesion molecules, may be a potential target for immunotherapy of colorectal cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high expression of the enzyme C2Gn T1, which catalyzes C2-O-slex synthesis, may be a useful marker of metastatic potential in colorectal adenomatous carcinomas.
C2Gn1 mRNA is highly upregulated during colorectal adenocarcioma progression, suggesting that C2Gnt1 is a key enzyme in the biosynthetic pathway of C2-O-Slex.
